title: Duke's nickname and the offer to play in London
summary: Ellington gets a call to play the Palladium in London and tells the band; Scott hesitates about family.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, I stayed with Duke -- I'm coming to that. I stayed with Duke and we made records and records and records. And finally, Duke got a call from overseas to play at the Royal Palladium in London. And Duke told me -- and I'll tell you, Duke was a guy -- he had such a nice disposition, he was a swell fellow. And he carried himself so nicely. That's why that nickname, Duke. He got that name. His real name was Edward, but he got that nickname in Washington, D.C. That was his home. And the way he carried himself was so nice.
So when he told us about it and said we're going to leave so-and-so and so-and-so, I said to myself, now, I'm
helping my father with the family. Can I say this?
